meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Да это не воровство, послушай! Это абсолютно безопасно.
examples.trans: That's not stealing, listen! It's completely safe.

meanings.note: medical institution for inpatient care

examples.trans: Everyone thinks you're in the hospital.
He was admitted to the hospital.

examples.text: Все думают, ты в больнице. Откуда деньги?
examples.trans: Everyone thinks you're in the hospital. Where did the money come from?

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Polite (вы) or plural. Core Russian det meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

влезть.gloss: to climb in, break into, get into

meanings.en: to climb into, break into, enter secretly
meanings.note: Perfective verb. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to climb in, break into, get into', paired with 'влезать'.

examples.text: В мой дом влезли чужие люди!
Кот ловко влез на высокое дерево.
examples.trans: The cat deftly climbed up the tall tree.

examples.text: Алло, полиция? В мой дом влезли!
examples.trans: Hello, police? Someone broke into my home!

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'memory, recollection' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a warm childhood memory.

meanings.note: Core Russian part meaning 'even' in everyday speech.
condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to defend, protect', paired with 'защитить'.

examples.trans: There is such a profession — defending the motherland!

examples.text: Мы готовы надёжно защищать вас везде.
examples.trans: We are ready to reliably protect you everywhere.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'anger, malice, spite' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я защищаю человека от твоей злости.
examples.trans: I protect a person from your anger.
Anger could be heard in his voice.

examples.text: Очень слабо, Лёва, нужно больше злости!
examples.trans: Very weak, Leva, we need more anger!

meanings.note: Damage something or ruin relations. Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'портить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to spoil, ruin, damage', paired with 'портить'.

examples.text: А я испорчу отношения с будущим мэром.
examples.trans: And I'll ruin my relationship with the future mayor.

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
кого + instrumental: назвать меня плохим словом
Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'звать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call, to name', paired with 'называть'.

examples.trans: You called me a bad word.
What will you name your son?

examples.text: Ты назвал меня плохим словом. Меня, начальника!
examples.trans: You called me a bad word. Me, your boss!

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'медленно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'чего').

examples.text: В таком случае мне здесь больше нечего делать.
examples.trans: In that case, there is nothing left for me to do here.
There is nothing to do here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам очень дорого обходится авторская кухня.
examples.trans: Auteur cuisine costs us very dearly.

examples.text: Это все, кто выходил из отеля.
examples.trans: That is everyone who left the hotel.
What is going on here right now?

meanings.note: Conclusively and without change. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Я окончательно ушёл от своей жены Аллы.
examples.trans: I have finally left my wife Alla.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: ничего не осталось = there's nothing left

Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remain, to be left', paired with 'оставаться'.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'from; of' in everyday speech.
Тошнит от = sick of. Core Russian prep meaning 'from; of' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

отойти.gloss: to step back, to move away

meanings.en: to step aside, to move back
meanings.note: Perfective of отходить. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to step back, to move away', paired with 'отходить'.

examples.trans: He stepped over to the window.
Step back! No comment! No comment!

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: портить настроение = ruin someone's mood

examples.text: Так, не портите мне прекрасное настроение.
examples.trans: Right, don't ruin my wonderful mood.

examples.text: Поверьте, вам это не надо. Вы так карму портите.
examples.trans: Believe us, you do not need this. You ruin your karma that way.

meanings.note: Short form: ты прав = you're right. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('right (side)').
Short form: ты прав = you're right. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('right (side)').

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

meanings.en: to talk, to speak, to have a conversation
meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'говаривать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to talk, to speak'.

examples.trans: Why are you talking so rudely?

examples.text: А что вы так грубо разговариваете?
examples.trans: Why are you talking so rudely?

meanings.note: Cause ruin to a family or thing. Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'рушить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to destroy, to ruin', paired with 'разрушать'.

examples.text: Ты разрушил мою семью своими фотографиями!
examples.trans: You destroyed my family with your photos!

examples.text: Ты разрушил такой прекрасный и сентиментальный момент!
examples.trans: You ruined such a wonderful and sentimental moment!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'ruin' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: От вашей семьи остались одни руины.
examples.trans: Only ruins remained of your family.

meanings.note: Жать руку = to shake hands. Common feminine noun meaning 'hand; arm' in everyday Russian.
+ instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'family' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Так, семья Самсоновых. Он строитель, она медсестра.
examples.trans: Right, the Samsonov family. He's a builder, she's a nurse.

meanings.en: to save, to rescue from danger
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to save, to rescue', paired with 'спасти'.

examples.text: Все прибежали тебя спасать — и я, и папа!
examples.trans: Everyone came running to save you — both me and Dad!
She is saving you from the hospital!

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

тронуть.gloss: to touch, lay a finger on

meanings.en: to touch, lay a finger on (someone)
meanings.note: Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to touch, lay a finger on', paired with 'трогать'.

examples.trans: Just lay one finger on him!

examples.text: Только тронь его пальцем! Мы всегда рады видеть Даню здесь.
examples.trans: Just lay a finger on him! We're always glad to see Danya here.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.
Possession. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.
Просить у кого. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to hit, strike', paired with 'ударять'.

examples.text: Вот если бы он ребёнка ударил!
examples.trans: Now if he had hit a child!
He hit the table with his fist.

examples.text: Меня всё ребёнок не отпускает. Вот если бы он ребёнка ударил!
examples.trans: I can't stop thinking about a child. Now if he had hit a child!

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'красть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to steal', paired with 'красть'.

examples.text: Чтобы он вернул деньги, которые украл.
examples.trans: For him to give back the money he stole.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Plural люди, a different word. Common masculine noun meaning 'person; (pl) people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
